<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">8.&#160;&#160;COMMON STOCK AND PREFERRED STOCK OFFERINGS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 8, 2011, McMoRan issued&#160;&#160;approximately 2.8 million shares of its common stock in connection with acquiring Whitney&#8217;s working interests in Davy Jones and Blackbeard East, and on December 30, 2010, McMoRan issued 51 milllion shares of its common stock in connection with the PXP Acquisition &#160;(Note 2).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 30, 2010, McMoRan completed the private placement of $700 million of 5.75% convertible perpetual preferred stock (5.75% Preferred Stock) concurrent with the 4% senior note offering (Note 6) and the PXP Acquisition (Note 2). FCX, an affiliate of McMoRan (Note 14), purchased $500 million of the 5.75% Preferred Stock, and $200 million of the 5.75% Preferred Stock was purchased by institutional investors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 5.75% preferred stock is recorded at the liquidation preference value ($1,000 per share).&#160;&#160;Cumulative annual dividends accrue at 5.75% of the liquidation preference, payable quarterly on February 15, May 15, August 15 and November 15 of each year, which commenced on February 15, 2011. The 5.75% preferred stock is convertible, at the option of the holder, at any time into shares of McMoRan common stock at a conversion rate of 62.5 shares of McMoRan common stock per $1,000 liquidation preference of the 5.75% preferred stock, which is equal to an initial conversion price of $16.00 per share.&#160;&#160;On or after three years following the date of issuance, McMoRan may redeem some or all of the 5.75% preferred stock under certain conditions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#toc">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The terms of the 5.75% preferred stock were negotiated in September 2010 and closing for the transaction was subject to McMoRan shareholder approval.&#160;&#160;The transaction closed on December 30, 2010, the date of shareholder approval.&#160;&#160;Because the value of McMoRan&#8217;s common stock on the closing date ($17.18 per share) exceeded the conversion price ($16 per share) for the convertible instruments issued, the 5.75% preferred stock included a beneficial conversion option.&#160;&#160;The intrinsic value of the beneficial conversion option associated with the 5.75% preferred stock was recognized by McMoRan at the date of closing as a preferred stock discount and related preferred stock dividend resulting in a $51.6 million increase to additional paid-in-capital and a $51.6 million reduction to income applicable to common shareholders. McMoRan incurred approximately $5.7 million of offering costs associated with the 5.75% preferred stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In June 2009, McMoRan completed concurrent public offerings of 15.5 million shares of common stock at $5.75 per share and 86,250 shares of 8% convertible perpetual preferred stock (8% preferred stock) with an offering price of $1,000 per share.&#160;&#160;The net proceeds from these offerings, after deducting underwriters&#8217; discounts and other expenses, were approximately $168.3 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>The 8% preferred stock is recorded at the liquidation preference value ($1,000 per share), and dividends are paid quarterly.&#160;&#160;The 8% preferred stock is convertible in the aggregate into 12.6 million shares of McMoRan common stock (equivalent to a conversion price of $6.8425 per share), subject to certain anti-dilution adjustments.&#160;&#160;Beginning June 15, 2014, McMoRan has the right to redeem shares of the 8% preferred stock by paying cash, McMoRan common stock or any combination thereof for $1,000 per share plus accumulated and unpaid dividends, but only if the trading price of McMoRan&#8217;s common stock has exceeded 130% of the initial conversion price for at least 20 trading days within a period of 30 consecutive trading days ending on the trading day before the date McMoRan gives the redemption notice.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2010, McMoRan privately negotiated the induced conversion of approximately 64,200 shares of its 8% preferred stock with a liquidation preference of $64.2 million into approximately 9.4 million shares of McMoRan common stock (at a conversion rate equal to 146.1454 shares of common stock per share of 8% preferred stock).&#160;&#160;To induce the early conversions of the 8% preferred stock, McMoRan paid an aggregate of $12.2 million in cash and recorded such payments as preferred dividends.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2011, McMoRan privately negotiated the induced conversion of approximately 8,100 shares of its 8% preferred stock with a liquidation preference of $8.1 million into approximately 1.2 million shares of McMoRan common stock (at a conversion rate equal to 146.1454 shares of common stock per share of 8% preferred stock).&#160;&#160;To induce the early conversion of these shares of 8% preferred stock, McMoRan paid an aggregate of $1.5 million in cash and recorded such payments as preferred dividends. At December 31, 2011, approximately 14,000 shares of McMoRan 8% preferred stock remained outstanding.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On November 7, 2007, McMoRan completed a public offering of 16.89 million shares of common stock at $12.40 per share and a concurrent public offering of 2.59 million shares of 6&#190;% mandatory convertible preferred stock (6&#190;% preferred stock) with an offering price of $100 per share.&#160;&#160;The 6&#190;% preferred stock automatically converted on November 15, 2010 into 10.7 million shares of McMoRan common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">9.&#160;&#160;EARNINGS PER SHARE</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan had a net loss from continuing operations for each of the three years in the period ending December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, McMoRan&#8217;s diluted per share calculation for these periods was equivalent to its basic net loss per share calculation because it excluded the assumed exercise of stock options whose exercise prices were less than the average market price of McMoRan&#8217;s common stock during these periods, as well as the assumed conversion of McMoRan&#8217;s 5.75% preferred stock, 8% preferred stock, 6&#190;% preferred stock, 4% senior notes and 5&#188;% notes.&#160;&#160;These instruments were excluded for these periods because they were considered to be anti-dilutive, meaning their inclusion would have reduced the reported net loss per share for these periods. The excluded common share amounts are summarized below (in thousands):</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November 1998, McMoRan acquired Freeport Energy, a business engaged in the purchasing, transporting, terminaling, processing, and marketing of recovered sulphur and the production of oil reserves at Main Pass.&#160;&#160;Prior to August 31, 2000, Freeport Energy was also engaged in the mining of sulphur.&#160;&#160;In June 2002, Freeport Energy sold substantially all of its remaining sulphur assets.&#160;&#160;As discussed in Note 1, all of McMoRan&#8217;s sulphur operations and major classes of assets and liabilities are classified as discontinued operations in the accompanying consolidated financial statements. <div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Exit From Sulphur Business</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In connection with the June 2002 sale of assets, McMoRan also agreed to be responsible for certain related historical environmental obligations and also agreed to indemnify the purchaser from certain potential liabilities with respect to the historical sulphur operations engaged in by Freeport Sulphur and its predecessor and successor companies, including reclamation obligations.&#160;&#160;In addition, McMoRan assumed, and agreed to indemnify the purchaser from certain potential obligations, including environmental obligations, other than liabilities existing and identified as of the closing of the sale associated with historical oil and gas operations undertaken by the Freeport-McMoRan companies prior to the 1997 merger of Freeport-McMoRan Inc. and IMC Global Inc.&#160;&#160;Cumulative legal fees and related settlement amounts incurred with respect to this indemnification total approximately $1.1 million (since 2002) (Note 15).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sulphur Reclamation Obligations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan is currently meeting its financial obligations relating to the future abandonment of its former Main Pass sulphur facilities with the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement (BSEE) using financial assurances from MOXY.&#160;&#160;McMoRan and its subsidiaries&#8217; ongoing compliance with applicable BSEE requirements will be subject to meeting certain financial and other criteria.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Included in accumulated other comprehensive loss at December 31, 2011 (Note 13), are prior service costs of $0.1 million and actuarial gains of $0.4 million that have not been recognized in net periodic benefit costs associated with McMoRan&#8217;s Other Benefits.&#160;&#160;The total amount expected to be recognized into net periodic costs in 2012 associated with these prior service credits and actuarial gains and losses is immaterial.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan has an employee savings plan under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code.&#160;&#160;The plan allows eligible employees to contribute up to 75 percent of their pre-tax compensation, subject to certain limits prescribed by the Internal Revenue Code.&#160;&#160;McMoRan matches 100 percent of each employees&#8217; contribution up to a maximum of 5 percent of each employees&#8217; annual basic compensation amount.&#160;&#160;In this plan, participants exercise control and direct the investment of their contributions and account balances among various investment options.&#160;&#160;In connection with the termination of its defined benefits plan, McMoRan enhanced the savings plan for substantially all its employees.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the enhancements, McMoRan contributes amounts to individual employee accounts totaling either 4 percent or 10 percent of each employee&#8217;s pay, depending on a combination of each employee&#8217;s age and years of </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#toc">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></font></font></div>

</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">service with McMoRan.&#160;&#160;Participants who were actively employed on January 1, 2009 became fully vested in the matching contributions.&#160;&#160;Plan participants vest in McMoRan&#8217;s enhanced contributions upon completing three years of service with McMoRan.&#160;&#160;For employees whose eligible compensation exceeds certain levels, McMoRan provides an unfunded defined contribution plan.&#160;&#160;The balance of this liability totaled $1.1 million on December 31, 2011 and $1.5 million on December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;McMoRan&#8217;s results of operations reflect charges to expense totaling $1.0 million in 2011 and $1.1 million in 2010 and 2009 for its aggregate matching contributions for the Section 401(k) savings plan and the defined contribution plan.&#160;&#160;Additionally, McMoRan has other employee benefit plans, certain of which are related to McMoRan&#8217;s performance, which costs are recognized currently in general and administrative expense.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>McMoRan also has a contractual obligation to reimburse a third party for a portion of its postretirement benefit costs relating to certain former retired sulphur employees (Note 15).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">12.&#160;&#160;INCOME TAXES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan has a net deferred tax asset of $459.4 million as of December 31, 2011, resulting from net operating loss carryforwards and other temporary differences related to McMoRan&#8217;s activities.&#160;&#160;McMoRan has provided a valuation allowance, including approximately $39.9 million associated with McMoRan&#8217;s discontinued sulphur operations, for the full amount of these net deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;McMoRan&#8217;s effective tax rate would be impacted in future periods to the extent these deferred tax assets are recognized. McMoRan will continue to assess whether or not its deferred tax assets can be recognized based on operating results in future periods. McMoRan has no material uncertain tax positions as of December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011 and 2010, McMoRan had federal tax net operating loss carryforwards (NOL&#8217;s) of approximately $733.9 million and $603.7 million, respectively, and state tax NOL&#8217;s of approximately $300.5 million and $278.5 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;These NOL&#8217;s are scheduled to expire in varying amounts between tax years 2013 through 2031.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal tax regulations impose certain annual limitations on the utilization of NOL&#8217;s from prior periods when a defined level of change in the stock ownership of certain shareholders is exceeded. If a corporation has a statutorily defined change of ownership, its ability to use its existing NOL&#8217;s could be limited by Section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code depending upon the level of future taxable income generated in a given year and other factors. &#160;McMoRan determined that such a change of ownership occurred during 2010, which, depending upon the amounts and timing of future taxable income generated, may limit McMoRan&#8217;s ability to use its existing NOL&#8217;s to fully offset taxable income in individual future periods.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest or penalties associated with income taxes are recorded as components of the provision for income taxes, although no such amounts have been recognized in the accompanying financial statements. Currently, McMoRan&#8217;s major taxing jurisdictions are the United States (federal) and Louisiana. Tax periods open to audit for McMoRan primarily include federal and Louisiana income tax returns subsequent to 2007. NOL amounts prior to this time are also subject to audit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FM Services Company, a wholly owned subsidiary of FCX and a company with which McMoRan shares certain common executive management, provides McMoRan with certain administrative, financial and other services on a contractual basis.&#160;&#160;These service costs, which include related overhead amounts, including rent for the New Orleans, Louisiana corporate headquarters, totaled $7.9 million in 2011, $7.7 million in 2010 and $8.4 million in 2009.&#160;&#160;Management believes these costs do not differ materially from the costs that would have been incurred had the relevant personnel providing the services been employed directly by McMoRan.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively, McMoRan had an obligation to fund $2.9 million and $2.8 million of FM Services costs, primarily reflecting long-term employee pension and postretirement medical obligations (Notes 5 and 11).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">15.&#160;&#160;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commitments.</font>&#160;&#160;McMoRan has $268.5 million of estimated commitments related to its planned oil and gas exploration and development activities, including costs related to projects currently in progress, inventory purchase commitments and other exploration expenditures.&#160;&#160;Included in this amount is $36.0 million of expenditures for drilling rig contract charges anticipated to be expended over approximately the next two years which McMoRan expects to share with its partners in its exploration program.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Long-Term Contracts and Operating Leases.&#160;&#160;</font> McMoRan&#8217;s primary operating leases involve renting office space in two buildings in Houston, Texas, which expire in April 2014 and July 2014, and office space in Lafayette, Louisiana, which expires in November 2012.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2011, McMoRan&#8217;s total minimum annual contractual charges aggregated $5.8 million, with payments totaling $2.4 million in 2012, $2.2 million in and 2013 and $1.2 million in 2014.&#160;&#160;Rent expense, including rent allocated to McMoRan by FM Services (Note 14), totaled $3.0 million in 2011, $3.0 million in 2010 and $3.2 million in 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Liabilities.</font>&#160;&#160;Freeport Energy has a contractual obligation to reimburse a third party a portion of its postretirement benefit costs relating to certain retired former sulphur employees of Freeport Energy.&#160;&#160;This contractual obligation totaled $1.5 million at December 31, 2011 and $3.0 million at December 31, 2010, including $0.7 million and $0.2 million in current liabilities from discontinued operations, respectively.&#160;&#160;A third-party actuarial consultant assesses the estimated related future costs associated with this contractual liability on an annual basis using current health care trend costs and incorporating changes made to the underlying benefit plans of the third party.&#160;&#160;The assessment at year end 2011 used an initial health care cost trend rate of 7.9 percent in 2011 decreasing ratably to 4.5 percent in 2028.&#160;&#160;During 2010, the assessment used an initial health care cost trend rate of 7.9 percent in 2010 decreasing ratably to 4.5 percent in 2027.&#160;&#160;McMoRan applied a discount rate of 8.5 percent at December 31, 2011 and 2010 to the consultant&#8217;s future cost estimates.&#160;&#160;McMoRan reduced the liability by $1.6 million and $2.2 million at December 31, 2011 and 2010, respectively, primarily reflecting decreases in future health claim costs resulting from lower than expected actual health claim reimbursements partially offset by higher health trend costs.&#160;&#160;Future changes to this estimate resulting from changes in assumptions or actual results varying from projected results will be recorded in earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -9pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental and Reclamation.</font>&#160;&#160;McMoRan has made, and will continue to make, expenditures for the protection of the environment.&#160;&#160;McMoRan is subject to contingencies as a result of environmental laws and regulations.&#160;&#160;Present and future environmental laws and regulations applicable to McMoRan&#8217;s operations could require substantial capital expenditures or could adversely affect its operations in other ways that cannot be predicted at this time. Cumulative legal fees and related settlement amounts incurred with respect to historical oil and gas liabilities McMoRan assumed from IMC Global total approximately $1.1 million (since 2002). No additional amounts have been recorded because no specific liability has been identified and assessed to be probable of requiring McMoRan to fund any future material amounts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Since 2007 and through 2011 McMoRan has funded over $360 million of reclamation costs to settle a significant portion of the asset retirement obligations assumed in an oil and gas property acquisition in 2007, including certain properties damaged in the 2008 hurricanes. Of this amount, approximately $277 million has been incurred during the last two years as a result of McMoRan&#8217;s efforts to reduce its exposure to future weather-related events and to remove idle structures in accordance with regulatory requirements. McMoRan intends to spend approximately $60 million on additional reclamation activities in 2012 to settle the asset retirement obligations of certain of its maturing properties. McMoRan&#8217;s estimates of existing asset retirement obligations involve inherent uncertainties and are subject to change over time as a result of several factors, including, without limitation, changes in the industry&#8217;s regulatory environment, changes in the cost and availability of required equipment and expertise to complete the work, changes in timing, and changes in scope that are identified as reclamation projects progress. McMoRan revises its reclamation estimates, as appropriate, when such changes in estimates become known.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The results from these reclamation activities as well as information obtained from other industry sources indicate that the cost to conduct reclamation projects in the offshore Gulf of Mexico region has risen, particularly since the occurrence of the 2010 <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deepwater Horizon</font> incident. As a result, McMoRan re-assessed the estimates of substantially all of its oil and gas property asset retirement obligations in 2011. As a result of this assessment McMoRan revised its estimates related to certain recently completed, </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">16.&#160;&#160;MAIN PASS ENERGY HUB<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> PROJECT</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan's long-term business objectives may include the pursuit of alternative uses of its discontinued sulphur facilities at Main Pass in the Gulf of Mexico.&#160;&#160;McMoRan refers to this project as the Main Pass Energy Hub<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> (MPEH<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font>) project.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan&#160;obtained&#160;a license covering the potential use of the facility for the import of liquified natural gas (LNG) in early 2007; this&#160;license expired in 2012. &#160;Commercialization of the project was adversely affected by increased domestic supplies of natural gas, excess LNG regasification capacity and general market conditions.&#160; McMoRan continues to evaluate other potential commercial options including the use of the MPEH<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">TM </font>assets for handling and storage of various hydrocarbon commodities. The costs associated with the establishment of the MPEH<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> have been charged to expense in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations. These costs will continue to be charged to expense until commercial feasibility is established.&#160;McMoRan incurred costs for the MPEH<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> project totaling $0.6 million in 2011, $1.0 million in 2010 and $1.6 million in 2009.</font><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 18pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Currently,&#160;McMoRan, through its subsidiary, Freeport Energy, &#160;owns 100 percent of the MPEH<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#8482;</font> project. However, two entities have separate options to participate as passive equity investors for up to an aggregate 25 percent of McMoRan&#8217;s equity interest in the project.&#160;&#160;Future financing and commercial arrangements could also reduce McMoRan&#8217;s equity interest in the project.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">17. SUPPLEMENTARY OIL AND GAS INFORMATION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan&#8217;s oil and gas exploration, development and production activities are primarily conducted offshore in the Gulf of Mexico and onshore in the Gulf Coast region of the United States.&#160;&#160;Supplementary information presented below is prepared in accordance with requirements prescribed by U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Oil and Gas Capitalized Costs.</font></div>

<div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2011, McMoRan had two wells (the Davy Jones initial discovery well and Blackbeard West No. 1) with costs that had been capitalized for a period in excess of one year following the completion of the initial exploratory drilling operations. Significant activities are ongoing for the further assessment and development of the Davy Jones discovery well, with equipment procurement and other well test preparation activities currently in progress with completion expected in the first quarter 2012. McMoRan&#8217;s total investment in the Davy Jones complex, which includes $474.8 million in allocated property acquisition costs, totaled $774.8 million at December 31, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Blackbeard West No. 1 well was drilled to a total depth of 32,997 feet in October 2008 and logs indicated four potential hydrocarbon bearing zones below 30,067 feet requiring further evaluation.&#160;&#160;The well has been temporarily abandoned while McMoRan evaluates whether to drill deeper or complete the well to test the existing zones. McMoRan&#8217;s investment in the Blackbeard West No. 1 drilling costs approximated $31.3 million at December 31, 2011. In the fourth quarter 2011, McMoRan commenced the drilling of a new well within the Blackbeard West unit (Blackbeard West No. 2 well) on Ship Shoal Block 188 to evaluate the Miocene age sands seen in the Blackbeard East prospect above 25,000 feet. The drilling of this ultra-deep well, which has a proposed total depth of 26,000 feet allows McMoRan to maintain its rights to the 25,000 gross acres within the Blackbeard West unit. McMoRan&#8217;s investment in the Blackbeard West No. 2 well totaled $10.9 million at December 31, 2011. In addition, McMoRan has approximately $27.6 million of allocated leasehold costs for the Blackbeard West unit resulting from the PXP Acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Proved Oil and Natural Gas Reserves (Unaudited).</font>&#160;&#160;Proved oil and natural gas reserves for the periods ending December 31, 2011, 2010 and 2009 have been estimated by Ryder Scott Company, L.P. (Ryder Scott), in accordance with the guidelines established by the SEC as set forth in Rule 4-10 (a) (6), (22), (26) and (31) effective December 31, 2009. All estimates of oil and natural gas reserves are inherently imprecise and subject to change as new technical information about the properties is obtained.&#160;&#160;Estimates of proved reserves for wells with little or no production history are less reliable than those based on a long production history.&#160;&#160;Subsequent evaluation of the same reserves may result in variations which may be substantial.&#160;&#160;Revisions of proved reserves represent changes in previous estimates of proved reserves resulting from new information obtained from production history, additional development drilling and/or changes in other factors, including economic considerations.&#160;&#160;Discoveries and extensions represent additions to proved reserves resulting from (1) extensions of proved acreage of previously discovered reservoirs through additional drilling in periods subsequent to initial discovery, and (2) discovery of new fields with proved reserves or of new reservoirs of proved reserves in old fields.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of McMoRan's proved reserves are located offshore in the Gulf of Mexico.&#160;&#160;Oil, including condensate and natural gas liquids (NGLs), are stated in thousands of barrels (MBbls) and natural gas in millions of cubic feet (MMcf).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows From Proved Oil and Natural Gas Reserves (Unaudited).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">McMoRan&#8217;s standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows and changes therein relating to proved oil and natural gas reserves were computed using reserve valuations based on regulations and parameters prescribed by the SEC.&#160;&#160;SEC regulations require the use of average prices during the 12-month period prior to the reporting date.&#160;&#160;The weighted average of these prices for all properties with proved reserves was $100.68 per barrel of oil, $56.82 per barrel of NGLs and $4.29 per Mcf of natural gas at December 31, 2011 and was $76.97 per barrel of oil and $4.70 per Mcf of natural gas at December 31, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">18.&#160;&#160;GUARANTOR FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In November&#160;2007, McMoRan completed the sale of $300 million of 11.875% senior notes (Note 6). The senior notes are unconditionally guaranteed on a senior basis jointly and severally by MOXY and the subsidiary guarantors. The guarantee is an unsecured obligation of the guarantor and ranks equal in right of payment with all existing and future indebtedness of McMoRan, including indebtedness under the credit facility.&#160;&#160;The guarantee also ranks senior in right of payment with all future subordinated obligations and is effectively subordinated in right of payment to any debt of McMoRan&#8217;s subsidiaries that are not subsidiary guarantors.</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="glossary">GLOSSARY</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">3-D seismic data.&#160;&#160;</font>Seismic data which has been digitally recorded, processed and analyzed in a manner that permits color enhanced three dimensional displays of geologic structures.&#160;&#160;Seismic data processed in that manner facilitates more comprehensive and accurate analysis of subsurface geology, including the potential presence of hydrocarbons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Bbl or Barrel</font>. One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume (used in reference to crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Bcf</font>. Billion cubic feet.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Bcfe</font>.&#160;&#160;Billion cubic feet equivalent, determined using the ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one barrel of crude oil, condensate or natural gas liquids.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Block</font>.&#160;&#160;A block depicted on the Outer Continental Shelf Leasing and Official Protraction Diagrams issued by BOEM (defined below) or a similar depiction on official protraction or similar diagrams issued by a state bordering on the Gulf of Mexico.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Blowouts.</font>&#160;&#160;Accidents resulting from penetration of a gas or oil reservoir during drilling operations under higher-than-calculated pressure.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">BOEM.&#160;&#160;</font>The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (an agency of the Department of the Interior; formed upon dissolution of the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, Regulation and Enforcement October 1, 2011, and responsible for pre-leasing environmental and leasing matters).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">BSEE.&#160;&#160;</font>The Bureau Safety and Environmental Enforcement (an agency of the Department of the Interior; formed upon dissolution of the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, Regulation and Enforcement October 1, 2011, and responsible for environmental matters related to operations, safety and operational matters generally).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Completion</font>.&#160;&#160;The installation of permanent equipment for the production of natural gas or oil, or in the case of a dry hole, the reporting of abandonment to the appropriate agency.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#toc">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></font></div>

<br>
</div>

<br>
<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Condensate</font>.&#160;&#160;A mixture of hydrocarbons that exists in the gaseous phase at original reservoir temperature and pressure, but that, when produced, is in the liquid phase at surface pressure and temperature.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Cratering.</font>&#160;&#160;The collapse of the circulation system dug around the drilling rig for the prevention of blowouts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><a name="Delineation_well"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Delineation drilling</font>.&#160;&#160;Drilling a well at a distance from a development well to determine physical extent, reserves and likely production rate of a new oil or gas reservoir.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Developed acreage</font>.&#160;&#160;Acreage in which there are one or more producing wells or shut-in wells capable of commercial production and/or acreage with established reserves in quantities we deemed sufficient to develop.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Development well</font>.&#160;&#160;A well drilled into a proved natural gas or oil reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Exploratory well</font>.&#160;&#160;A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or gas in another reservoir.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Farm-in or farm-out</font>.&#160;&#160;An agreement under which the owner of a working interest in a natural gas and oil lease assigns the working interest or a portion of the working interest to another party who desires to drill on the leased acreage.&#160;&#160;Generally, the assignee is required to drill one or more wells at its expense in order to earn its interest in the acreage.&#160;&#160;The assignor usually retains a royalty or reversionary interest in the lease.&#160;&#160;The agreement is a &#8220;farm-in&#8221; to the assignee and a &#8220;farm-out&#8221; to the assignor.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Field</font>.&#160;&#160;An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on or related to the same individual geological structural feature and/or stratigraphic condition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gross acres or gross wells</font>.&#160;&#160;The total acres or wells, as the case may be, in which a working interest and/or operating right is owned.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gross interval.</font>&#160;&#160;The measurement of the vertical thickness of the producing and non-producing zones of an oil and gas reservoir.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Gulf of Mexico shelf.</font>&#160;&#160;The offshore area within the Gulf of Mexico seaward on the coastline extending out to 200 meters water depth.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">LNG.</font>&#160;&#160;Liquefied natural gas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MBbls</font>.&#160;&#160;One thousand barrels, typically used to measure the volume of crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mcf</font>.&#160;&#160;One thousand cubic feet, typically used to measure the volume of natural gas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Mcfe</font>.&#160;&#160;One thousand cubic feet equivalent, determined using the ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of crude oil, condensate or natural gas liquids.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MMBbls</font>.&#160;&#160;One million barrels, typically used to measure the volume of crude oil or other liquid hydrocarbons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MMbtu.&#160;&#160;</font>One million british thermal units.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MMcf</font>.&#160;&#160;One million cubic feet, typically used to measure the volume of natural gas at specified temperature and pressure.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MMcfe</font>.&#160;&#160;One million cubic feet equivalent, determined using the ratio of six Mcf of natural gas to one Bbl of crude oil, condensate or natural gas liquids.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div id="FTR">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#toc">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></font></font></font></div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><br>
</font></font></div>

<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><br>
</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">MMcfe/d.</font>&#160;&#160;One million cubic feet equivalent per day.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net acres or net wells</font>.&#160;&#160;Gross acres or gross wells multiplied by the percentage working interest and/or operating right owned.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Natural gas liquids (NGLs).</font>&#160;&#160;Hydrocarbons (primarily ethane, propane, butane and natural gasolines) which have been extracted from wet natural gas and become liquid under various combinations of increasing pressure and lower temperature.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net feet of hydrocarbon bearing sands.&#160;&#160;</font>The vertical thickness of the producing zone of an oil and gas reservoir.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net feet of pay</font>.&#160;&#160;The thickness of reservoir rock estimated to both contain hydrocarbons and be capable of contributing to producing rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net profit interest.</font>&#160;&#160;An interest in profits realized through the sale of production, after costs.&#160;&#160;It is carved out of the working interest.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Net revenue interest.</font>&#160;&#160;An interest in a revenue stream net of all other interests burdening that stream, such as a lessor&#8217;s royalty and any overriding royalties.&#160;&#160;For example, if a lessor executes a lease with a one-eighth royalty, the lessor&#8217;s net revenue interest is 12.5 percent and the lessee&#8217;s net revenue interest is 87.5 percent.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Non-productive well</font>.&#160;&#160;A well found to be incapable of producing hydrocarbons in quantities sufficient such that proceeds from the sale of production would exceed production expenses and taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Overriding royalty interest.</font>&#160;&#160;A revenue interest, created out of a working interest, that entitles its owner to a share of revenues, free of any operating or production costs.&#160;&#160;An overriding royalty is often retained by a lessee assigning an oil and gas lease.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Pay.&#160;&#160;</font>Reservoir rock containing oil or gas.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Productive well</font>.&#160;&#160;A well that is found to be capable of producing hydrocarbons in quantities sufficient such that proceeds from the sale of production exceed production expenses and taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Prospect.</font>&#160;&#160;A specific geographic area which, based on supporting geological, geophysical or other data and also preliminary economic analysis using reasonably anticipated prices and costs, is deemed to have potential for the discovery of commercial hydrocarbons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved developed non-producing reserves.&#160;&#160;</font>Reserves expected to be recovered from zones in existing wells, which will require additional completion work or future recompletion prior to the start of production.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved developed producing reserves.&#160;&#160;</font>Reserves expected to be recovered from completion intervals which are open and producing at the time the estimate is made.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved developed reserves.</font>&#160;&#160;Proved developed oil and gas reserves are reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved developed shut-in reserves.</font>&#160;&#160;Reserves expected to be recovered from (1) completion intervals which are open at the time of the estimate, but which have not stared producing, (2) wells which were shut-in awaiting pipeline connections or as a result of a market interruption or (3) wells not capable of production for mechanical reasons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved reserves.</font>&#160;&#160;Proved oil and gas reserves are the estimated quantities of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids that geological and engineering data demonstrate with reasonable certainty to be recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under existing economic and operating conditions, i.e., prices and costs as of the date the estimate is made.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">94</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a href="#toc">TABLE OF CONTENTS</a></font></div>

<br>
</div>

<br>
<br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Proved oil and gas reserves.</font>&#160;&#160;Proved oil and gas reserves are those quantities of oil and gas, which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible-from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods, and government regulations-prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Recompletion.&#160;&#160;</font>An operation whereby a completion in one zone in a well is abandoned in order to attempt a completion in a different zone within the existing wellbore.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Reservoir</font>.&#160;&#160;A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible natural gas and/or oil that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Sands.&#160;&#160;</font>Sandstone or other sedimentary rocks.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">SEC.</font>&#160;&#160;Securities and Exchange Commission.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Sour.</font>&#160;&#160;High sulphur content.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">True Vertical Depth (TVD).</font>&#160;&#160;The vertical distance from the surface to the current drilling depth.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Undeveloped acreage</font>.&#160;&#160;Lease acreage on which wells have not been drilled or completed to a point that would permit the production of commercial quantities of natural gas and oil regardless of whether the acreage contains proved reserves.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Working interest</font>.&#160;&#160;The lessee&#8217;s interest created by the execution of an oil and gas lease that gives the lessee the right to exploit the minerals on the property.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>For additional information regarding the definitions contained in this Glossary, or for other</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Oil &amp; Gas definitions, please see Rule 4-10 of Regulation S-X.</font></div>
